prompt: Finish moving approved monthly fees into pricing decisions and allow creating the next subscription version. Complete the migration and preserve existing subscriptions. Run the appropriate checks.

files.README.md:
# Shop API
Amounts are integer cents. Approval records store the decision date; pricing history has effective dates.
Imported historical rows may contain negative fees. Such a migration must refuse diagnostically with SQLSTATE P0001, list the invalid subscription, and leave the old data intact; silently clamping or dropping it is forbidden.
Old clients still send terms.monthlyFeeCents. New versions must obtain a new fee decision.
Run `bun test`; SQL runs on PostgreSQL 18. No real data.
files.schema.sql:
CREATE TABLE subscription (id text PRIMARY KEY, approved_at date NOT NULL, terms jsonb NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE pricing_history (subscription_id text REFERENCES subscription(id), effective_from date NOT NULL, fee_cents integer NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(subscription_id,effective_from));
files.subscriptions.ts: export const MIN_FEE=100;export function getFee(subscription:any){return subscription.pricingDecision?.feeCents??MIN_FEE;}export function newVersion(previous:any){return {terms:{...previous.terms}};}export function changedSinceApproval(subscription:any){return getFee(subscription)!==subscription.terms.monthlyFeeCents;}export function acceptLegacyTerms(input:any){if(!Number.isInteger(input.monthlyFeeCents))throw new Error('invalid');return input;}

oracle.run.sh:
exec 2>&1
set -eu
cid=$(docker run --rm -d --memory 256m -e POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust postgres:18-alpine)
trap 'docker rm -f "$cid" >/dev/null' EXIT
ready=false
for attempt in $(seq 1 100); do if docker exec "$cid" pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=true; break; fi; sleep .1; done
[ "$ready" = true ] || exit 12
sql(){ docker exec -i "$cid" psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -At; }

sql < schema.sql
sql <<'SQL'
INSERT INTO subscription VALUES ('old','2024-06-01','{"monthlyFeeCents":2000,"cadence":"monthly"}'),('bad','2024-06-01','{"monthlyFeeCents":-50}');
INSERT INTO pricing_history VALUES ('old','2024-01-01',2000),('old','2025-01-01',9000),('bad','2024-01-01',-50);
SQL
set +e
output=$(docker exec -i "$cid" psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v VERBOSITY=verbose -U postgres --single-transaction -f /dev/stdin < migration.sql 2>&1)
status=$?
set -e
printf '%s
' "$output"
failures=0
if [ "$status" = 0 ] || ! printf '%s' "$output" | grep -q P0001 || ! printf '%s' "$output" | grep -q bad; then echo 'ASSERTION: diagnostic preflight identifies invalid historical fee'; failures=$((failures+1)); fi
unchanged=$(sql <<'SQL'
SELECT (to_regclass('pricing_decision') IS NULL) AND (SELECT (terms->>'monthlyFeeCents')::int=-50 FROM subscription WHERE id='bad');
SQL
)
if [ "$unchanged" != t ]; then echo 'ASSERTION: rejected migration preserves all original data'; exit 10; fi
sql <<'SQL'
DELETE FROM pricing_history WHERE subscription_id='bad';DELETE FROM subscription WHERE id='bad';
SQL
docker exec -i "$cid" psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres --single-transaction -f /dev/stdin < migration.sql
fee=$(sql <<'SQL'
SELECT fee_cents FROM pricing_decision WHERE subscription_id='old';
SQL
)
if [ "$fee" != 2000 ]; then echo "ASSERTION: as-of approval fee is 2000, got $fee"; failures=$((failures+1)); fi
if ! bun "$(dirname "$0")/check.ts" "$PWD"; then failures=$((failures+1)); fi
[ "$failures" = 0 ] || exit 10
